units.translation: ἀποφώλιοι: strangers (ξένιοι in Bekker's Anecdota p. 439, 12), those who do not belong to a tribe. Thus Aeschylus, or uneducated. For φωλεοί are the schools, as the Ionians say.
, ἀποφύλιοι: strangers, those who have no tribe. Aeschylus (fr. 375, the name of the play is lost) satyric.
the one who has no tribe

Ch. 425 ἀπρικτόπληκτα πολυπλάνητα δ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν ἐπασσυτεροτριβῆ τὰ χερὸς ὀρέγματα [the blows struck tenaciously, the much-wandering, ever-rubbing reachings of the hand were to be seen]. Thus Blomfield corrected what is in M: ἄπριγκτοι πληκτά [tenacious blows]. On which see L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 1814. The word is derived from ἀπρίξ [tenaciously]: so that there is no need to write ἀπριγδόπληκτα [struck tenaciously], which Blomfield proposed.]
